query: What hierarchical occlusion deletion/insertion protocols (replacement distribution, patch sizes per level, coarse-to-fine thresholds, and number of samples) minimize visual artifacts while preserving in-distribution statistics for 3D MRI?

response.query: What hierarchical occlusion deletion/insertion protocols (replacement distribution, patch sizes per level, coarse-to-fine thresholds, and number of samples) minimize visual artifacts while preserving in-distribution statistics for 3D MRI?
response.answer: Hierarchical occlusion protocols minimizing visual artifacts in 3D MRI use uniform patch sizes, adaptive coarse-to-fine thresholds, and balanced sample distributions to preserve in-distribution statistics. Optimal settings vary by dataset but typically involve small patch sizes and multiple levels of refinement.
